summary: Describes an optional extension to the Internet Printing Protocol 1.1 that lets a client subscribe to printing events, modeled as Subscription Objects that say what to do when a given event occurs.

eli5.summary: You can ask the printer to tell you when your job is done or paper runs out, instead of walking over to check.

questions: how to subscribe to printer events
what is the ippget delivery method
how long does an ipp subscription last
subtitle: How a print client asks a printer to report job and printer events, and how long that request lasts.

tldr.problem: A client that sends a job to an IPP printer has no standard way to learn when the job finishes, when the printer jams, or when its configuration changes, short of asking over and over.
tldr.mechanism: The client creates Subscription Objects on the printer that name the events it cares about, where or how to deliver them, and for how long. When a matching event occurs, the printer produces an Event Notification and either pushes it to a recipient or holds it for the recipient to pull.
tldr.outcome: The extension is OPTIONAL, but a printer or client that implements it must support the 'ippget' pull delivery method. It updates RFC 2910 and RFC 2911.

today: RFC 3995 is a Proposed Standard from March 2005. It updates RFC 2910 and RFC 2911, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Notification Model
sections.content:
RFC 3995 is an OPTIONAL extension to Internet Printing Protocol 1.1 (RFC 2911 and RFC 2910). It lets a client subscribe to printing-related Events, such as a job completing or a printer stopping. An Event is an instantaneous change of state, condition or configuration. A jam occurring and a jam clearing are two distinct Events.

A client creates a Subscription Object on the printer. The object says which Events matter, who receives the report, how it is delivered, and what the report contains. When one of those Events occurs, the printer delivers an Event Notification to the Notification Recipient, which can be the subscribing client or a third party.

This document does not define any delivery mechanism itself. Each Delivery Method lives in its own document, and this one requires only that clients and printers support the 'ippget' pull method from RFC 3996. It is meant to meet the most important requirements in RFC 3997, together with RFC 3381.
sections.eli5: You tell the printer what you want to hear about and who to tell. When something happens, the printer sends that person a short message.

sections.title: Subscription Objects and Their Relationships
sections.content:
There are two kinds of Subscription Object. A Per-Job object belongs to exactly one Job and lasts exactly as long as that Job. A Per-Printer object belongs to the Printer as a whole and has a lease. A Printer can have zero or more of the second kind, and a Job can have zero or more of the first.

Both kinds can subscribe to Job Events, Printer Events, or both. Both can be queried and cancelled in the same way. The difference is scope: Job Events in a Per-Job object apply only to its one Job, while Job Events in a Per-Printer object apply to all jobs on the Printer.

A client usually creates Per-Job objects while submitting the job, because the Create-Job-Subscriptions operation is OPTIONAL. Subscription attributes are split into Template attributes, which the client may supply and whose names start with notify-, and Description attributes, which only the printer sets, such as notify-subscription-id.
sections.eli5: One kind of note is stuck to a single page you printed. The other is stuck to the printer itself and covers everyone's pages.

sections.title: Events and Matching
sections.content:
The notify-events attribute holds the Subscribed Events. Some events are sub-values of others: job-completed is a sub-value of job-state-changed, and a subscriber to the parent hears about every child. Required Job events are job-state-changed, job-created and job-completed. Required Printer events are printer-state-changed and printer-stopped. The rest, such as job-progress, printer-media-changed and printer-queue-order-changed, are OPTIONAL. A printer MUST support at least 2 values per Subscription Object.

When a Printer Event occurs, every Per-Printer and Per-Job subscription that matches it produces a notification. When a Job Event occurs, every matching Per-Printer subscription does, but only the Per-Job subscriptions attached to that same Job do.

Two subscriptions that would yield identical notifications for the same recipient still each get one; the printer MUST NOT merge them. If one subscription matches an event twice (a value and its sub-value), the printer MAY send one notification or two.

For job-progress, notify-time-interval sets the minimum number of seconds between notifications, so a busy printer does not send one for every sheet.
sections.eli5: If you ask to hear about 'anything that happens to a job', you also hear when it finishes. Only a note stuck on your own page tells you about your page alone.

sections.title: Template Attributes, Leases and Sequence Numbers
sections.content:
A client supplies notify-recipient-uri for a push method or notify-pull-method for a pull method, never both. Other template attributes include notify-charset and notify-natural-language for text in notifications, notify-user-data for opaque data of at most 63 octets that the recipient gets back, and the optional notify-attributes for extra attributes in machine-readable notifications.

A Per-Printer object is kept alive by a lease. notify-lease-duration is in seconds, from 0 to 67108863, and 0 means the lease never expires. The printer may grant a different value than requested, and it deletes the object when the lease runs out. The client keeps it alive with Renew-Subscription. A Per-Job object has no lease.

The printer sets notify-subscription-id (a number starting at 1) and a notify-sequence-number that starts at 0 and increases by 1 with each notification. Gaps tell the recipient it missed a notification, and a repeat tells it about a duplicate.
sections.eli5: Your note on the printer has an expiry date, and you can ask for more time. Each message gets a number so you can tell if one went missing.

sections.title: Event Notification Content and Delivery Methods
sections.content:
This RFC lists what a notification contains, but each Delivery Method Document defines the exact format. A machine consumable notification MUST include the subscription id, the printer URI, the subscribed event and printer-up-time. For Job events it adds job-id, job-state and job-state-reasons. For Printer events it adds printer-state, printer-state-reasons and printer-is-accepting-jobs.

A human consumable notification is localized text that programs MUST NOT try to parse. Notifications from one Subscription Object MUST be in time stamp order.

With a push method the printer delivers shortly after the event. With a pull method it keeps notifications for the Event Life and the recipient fetches them. The recipient URI scheme names a push method, and the 'ippget' keyword names the required pull method. A Delivery Method Document must answer a fixed list of questions, such as transport, latency and security.

If an error would recur on every future delivery, such as a recipient address that does not exist, the printer MUST cancel the Subscription Object.
sections.eli5: Some messages are for computers and have fixed parts. Others are for people and are just a sentence. Either the printer drops the message off, or you come and pick it up.

sections.title: Operations for Subscriptions
sections.content:
Six new operations are added, and existing job creation operations (Print-Job, Print-URI, Create-Job) can carry subscription groups. Create-Printer-Subscriptions and the other new operations are REQUIRED. Create-Job-Subscriptions is OPTIONAL. Create-Job-Subscriptions needs a notify-job-id naming a job that has not completed.

  • Create-Printer-Subscriptions makes Per-Printer objects.
  • Create-Job-Subscriptions makes Per-Job objects for an existing job.
  • Get-Subscription-Attributes and Get-Subscriptions read one object or many.
  • Renew-Subscription extends a Per-Printer lease and is rejected for a Per-Job object.
  • Cancel-Subscription deletes an object and stops further notifications.

The response holds one Subscription Attributes Group per request group, in the same order. Failures are reported per group through notify-status-code, so a request can half succeed. In a job creation request a subscription failure MUST NOT make the job itself fail. The only attribute of an existing object that can be changed is the lease, so changing anything else means creating a new subscription and cancelling the old one.
sections.eli5: You can leave a note, read your notes, ask for more time, or tear a note up. If one note cannot be written, the others still get written.

sections.title: Access Rights and Security
sections.content:
Subscription requests carry the same security issues as submitting an IPP/1.1 print job, and the same mechanisms apply: HTTP authentication where authentication is needed and HTTP/TLS where privacy is needed. Access control follows the model for jobs. A job owner, an operator, an administrator, or someone authorized by the administrator's policy may create Per-Job objects, while creating Per-Printer objects needs operator or administrator rights or such authorization.

If subscription ids are assigned sequentially and there is no security, a passive observer can learn about the system. The RFC also warns that notify-attributes could become a trap door, so the printer MUST apply the same security policy to requested attributes as it does to other queries.

For any push method the biggest concern is unwanted notifications sent to third parties, in effect spam. The RFC notes that a fully secure solution would need the active agreement of all recipients, and each Delivery Method Document MUST discuss its own security considerations.
sections.eli5: Only the right people get to leave or read notes. The worry is someone telling the printer to send messages to a person who never asked for them.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content:
Implementing the whole specification is OPTIONAL. A client that does implement it MUST support the 'ippget' pull method as defined in RFC 3996 and MAY support others. A printer that implements it MUST meet the base IPP conformance requirements, support subscription groups in requests and responses, support the required attributes, support 'ippget', and deliver notifications that follow section 9 and the Delivery Method Document of each method it offers.

New values are added to operations-supported for the six operations, and two new attribute group tags are defined: 0x06 for the subscription attributes tag and 0x07 for the event notification attributes tag. The IANA section registers these and sets out how future Events and Delivery Methods are registered.
sections.eli5: You do not have to offer this feature. If you do, you must at least offer the pick-up kind of delivery so everybody can talk to everybody.
